messages:
alex: Heads-up — Compliance asked for stronger per-tenant routing-policy provenance. They want an audit artifact that shows who changed the routing policy for tenant T, the exact delta, and which fallback model/pool was used during the rollout. They also want this to be exportable as a signed bundle.
priya: We already emit change events into the audit stream but the gaps are: cross-tenant diffs (we don't collate related changes), PII in actor fields, and linking policy changes to quota/billing tags.
dylan: Quick Q: should exports contain full policy snapshots or just diffs + anchors that let you reconstruct a snapshot? For legal purposes deterministic full snapshots are easier to validate, but heavier.
jen: @dylan I'd prefer diffs in the console (human readable) and full snapshots available via export job (NDJSON bundle). Console/UI should show inline diff + timeline of canary -> ramp -> global. :eyes:
alex: Another sticky bit: quota & routing interplay. If a policy change reroutes to dedicated capacity, billing tags change and quota enforcement may switch product tiers. Audit needs to capture effective_tags at the time of change so revenue/compliance can reconcile.
priya: Proposal idea: add two fields to the audit event: `previous_effective_tags` and `new_effective_tags`. We can default to scrubbing PII (email addresses) but keep opaque actor IDs. For exports, allow a tenant-scoped opt-in to include unhashed actor email for internal legal teams.
dylan: Sample event shape (rough):
```
{
  "event_type":"routing.policy.update",
  "actor":"user:priya",
  "actor_id":"usr_abcdef",
  "tenant":"tenant-123",
  "timestamp":"2026-03-20T12:01:11Z",
  "before":"policy_v1",
  "after":"policy_v2",
  "previous_effective_tags":["pool:shared","quota:standard"],
  "new_effective_tags":["pool:dedicated-eu","quota:gold"],
  "rollout_stage":"canary",
  "signed_proof":"<signature-b64>"
}
```
jen: Signed proof is important. Who signs bundles? Backend HSM is my +1 — we shouldn't rely on the console client for signatures. Ops/security: can we attach a detached signature per export job and provide a verification endpoint?
ops-bot: export-service: signed bundle created, export_id=export-20260320-001, signing_key=kms-redwood-prod, status=ready :white_check_mark:
audit-bot: note: export-service applied redaction profile=pii-scrub; removed principal emails and replaced with `actor_id`. Full actor email requires tenant consent or enterprise support.
priya: Concrete path forward suggestion: 1) keep change events as diffs in the live audit stream for low-latency UX; 2) support on-demand NDJSON snapshot exports (full snapshot) signed by backend; 3) include `effective_tags` fields; 4) default export redaction to pii-scrub but allow enterprise opt-ins; 5) console shows inline diffs + rollout timeline and a link to signed export.
alex: Sounds reasonable. Can we also record which routing-policy-version was active per-minute for 30 days (time-series anchor) so we can answer "what rule was serving at 12:03:11"? That allows precise post-incident reconstructions.
dylan: I'll add a lightweight time-series anchor in the meta-store (one entry per policy change with start_ts, end_ts, active_tags). It'll be compact. ETA: next Tue.
jen: I'll mock the UI: two panes — left: compact diff + who/when/ack; right: timeline with rollout % and config snapshot link. Will post png here later. :thumbsup:
alex: OK — can someone open the API schema PR (audit event changes + export endpoints) and an RFC for console UX by Thursday EOD? I'll coordinate the compliance review.
priya: I'll start the schema PR and add tests for redaction modes.
jen: filing a UX RFC and attaching mock in this thread soon.
dylan: I'll include migration notes for consumers of the audit stream. Need to version events so downstream parsers don't break. Suggest `event_schema_version` on root.
alex: Thanks all. Filing a tracking ticket after this thread and tagging legal/compliance.
_reserved_notes: This thread mimics a short, realistic eng-platform Slack discussion. Messages are intentionally concise and include inline code, emoji, bot notices, and a small JSON snippet to reflect schema discussion.
